---
title: "Quality control"
---

Registration failure is the main risk in a cyclic-IF experiment, and it does
not always announce itself. A misaligned plate still produces a full dataset
and a plausible-looking plot — the numbers are simply from the wrong cells.

Run the QC report before trusting any 4i result.

```bash
python bin/alignment_qc.py 4126 -o alignment_qc
```

Pass several master plate IDs to treat them as biological replicates and add a
combined, replicate-level analysis.

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `-o, --outdir DIR` | `alignment_qc` | Destination for CSVs, tables and figures |
| `--sample-alignments` | off | **Must match how `aggregate_plates` was run** |
| `--iqr N` | 1.5 | IQR factor for per-well agreement outlier removal |
| `--mask-samples N` | 12 | Fields sampled for nuclear-mask overlap (0 to skip) |
| `--pixel-size N` | — | Override the pixel size |
| `--attach` | — | Attach the report back to the OMERO plate |
| `--seed N` | random | Random seed for sampling |
| `--env NAME` | — | Environment file to load |

## What the report contains

Everything for one run lands in a single directory: the raw input CSVs, the
derived metric tables, summary and statistics tables, and the figures. That
makes it archivable alongside the analysis — the evidence that a given dataset
was correctly registered travels with the dataset.

`--attach` additionally uploads the report to the OMERO plate, which is the
better choice when the analysis is shared.

## Reading the result

The two questions the report answers are whether individual rounds agree with
the reference, and whether that agreement is uniform across the plate.
Registration that is good in the plate centre and poor at the edges points at a
stage-position or stitching problem rather than a staining one.

`--mask-samples` controls how many fields are sampled for direct nuclear-mask
overlap. It requires downloading masks, so it is the slow part of the report;
set it to `0` for a quick pass and raise it when a plate looks suspect.
